scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and "fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills" (CL-01); this is the requester's framing of the solution, not the validated problem.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-04).
59% of disputed bills (1,785/3,025) carry ACTUAL read type rather than ESTIMATED (E-01).
Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05).
Dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) (E-03), so response capacity is not degraded.
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1,180-1,260/month starting August 2026 (E-04). The majority of disputed bills (59%, 1,785 of 3,025, E-01) carry ACTUAL (not estimated) read types, indicating a billing calculation or tariff-application defect in the billing-import step is producing wrong bills on normally-read accounts — independent of any tariff rate change (ruled out, E-02) and independent of response-time capacity (already within SLA, E-03). A separate, smaller mechanism — field manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target (E-05) — plausibly drives estimate substitution for the remaining minority of disputed (ESTIMATED-read) bills.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-11: E-01's observation (1,785 ACTUAL vs 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills, billing-db) still stands as the read-type split, but it no longer supports treating the ESTIMATED minority as attributable to field route-completion shortfall. E-11 shows that minority is dominantly explained by a billing-import REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rule rejecting valid AMI reads, leaving the ACTUAL-majority defect mechanism still unidentified.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

H-SLOW-RESPONSE-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response-capacity problem, solvable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets faster.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced misclassification or incorrect estimate substitution, producing wrong bills that drive disputes.

H-AMI-EXPORT-DEGRADATION.statement: The nightly AMI export from the vendor (ORG-AMI) degraded or became incomplete around August, causing more estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The manual meter-read handoff from the contracted field service (ORG-FIELD) degraded (missed uploads or incomplete routes), increasing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-BILLS-CORRECT-EXTERNAL-DRIVE.statement: Bills are largely accurate; the ticket surge stems from an external factor (e.g., tariff/rate change, seasonal usage shift, communication issue) unrelated to a data or process defect.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: A billing calculation or tariff-application defect affecting bills with ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads is driving the majority of disputes, independent of estimate substitution.

H-IMPORT-REJECTS-HIGH-CONSUMPT.statement: Billing import rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and substitutes an estimate instead of using the received read, driving the large majority of disputed ESTIMATED-read bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of disputed bills, 1785 carry read_type ACTUAL versus 1240 ESTIMATED (billing-db, E-01) — the majority of disputed bills (about 59% of the 3025 total) are not estimate-substituted reads. This means estimate-substitution-driven causes can explain at most a minority of disputed bills, and some other factor affects disputes on bills built from actual reads.

E-01's observation (1,785 ACTUAL vs 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills, billing-db) still stands as the read-type split, but it no longer supports treating the ESTIMATED minority as attributable to field route-completion shortfall. E-11 shows that minority is dominantly explained by a billing-import REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rule rejecting valid AMI reads, leaving the ACTUAL-majority defect mechanism still unidentified.

billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records (E-02), meaning no tariff/rate change was logged, so a tariff change cannot be the cause of the dispute surge or of billing errors on actual-read bills.

crm-tickets.dispute_response_times (E-03) reports median response 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets — tickets are on average being answered within SLA already. This speaks to response capacity/speed, not to why bills are disputed or why ticket volume doubled.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly (E-04) shows 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep) disputes — ticket count roughly doubled starting precisely in August, confirming the surge's timing and magnitude but saying nothing about its cause.

Route-log data (E-05) shows field route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9200 manual-read accounts during Aug-Sep 2026, a measurable manual-read collection shortfall coinciding with the dispute surge period. This provides a concrete data point for the field-handoff-degradation mechanism, but given E-01 shows most disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not estimated) reads, this shortfall can at most explain a portion of disputes tied to the smaller estimated-read population.

E-05's observation (88% route completion vs 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts, Aug-Sep 2026, route-log) still stands as a genuine field shortfall, but it no longer supports being even a partial cause of the ESTIMATED-read dispute population as a whole. E-11 shows 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED disputes had a valid AMI read exported but rejected by billing import, leaving only the 56 no-read cases plausibly tied to route completion.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, a stakeholder claim that agrees with the existing authoritative tool evidence E-02 (billing-db.tariff_change_log returned 0 records) already ruling out a tariff change as a cause.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager, non-authoritative) claims a three-reader staffing shortfall since July causes routes to run late, producing estimated bills for affected customers. This is a stakeholder claim offering a specific causal mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already observed in E-05, not independently verified data.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility may request field route priority changes, but such changes are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager — corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement on push_route_update rather than revealing anything about dispute causation.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) returns 14 distinct routes with varying completion rates (sample: R-00 at 0.70), giving a route-level breakdown of the aggregate 88%-vs-95% shortfall already seen in E-05. It confirms the shortfall is distributed across many routes but does not by itself identify why any route lags (staffing vs. other causes).

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which if true would unblock the previously access-pending mdms-export query and the PENDING request_vendor_export_access work item. The observation says nothing about actual AMI read-event content, export reliability, or billing-defect causation — it is only an access-status claim, not evidence resolving any causal question.

mdms-export's read_events_for_disputed_estimated (E-11) shows that of AMI-channel reads tied to the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1,184 had a valid read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (forcing estimate substitution despite a valid read), while 56 had no AMI read received at all. This points to a billing-import validation rule rejecting high-consumption AMI reads as the dominant mechanism behind the ESTIMATED-read dispute population, rather than field manual-read route-completion failure.

U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: What specific billing calculation or tariff-application defect in the import/validation step is producing wrong bills on ACTUAL-read accounts?
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Without identifying the mechanism, no corrective change can be validated as actually fixing the ACTUAL-read bill errors.
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Review billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) and sample disputed ACTUAL-read bills in billing-db (DA-BILL) to isolate the defect.
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Proceed only with diagnostic actions (investigate_billing_rule_change, analyze_disputed_bills_by_cause); no bill correction is proposed until the mechanism is confirmed.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-UNVERIF.question: Is the field reader staffing shortage SH-FIELD cites (E-07) actually the cause of the route-completion shortfall, or are there other causes?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-UNVERIF.decision_impact: Affects whether a route-priority push targets the actual root cause of the route-completion shortfall or only a symptom of it.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-UNVERIF.resolution_path: Obtain independent field-service staffing/headcount records to verify SH-FIELD's staffing-shortage claim beyond the stakeholder statement E-07.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-UNVERIF.safe_placeholder: Treat the staffing claim as unverified; any push_route_update still requires K-DISPATCH Field Operations Manager runtime confirmation regardless of the underlying cause.

U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH-UNRESOLVED.question: Does AMI export degradation contribute to estimate substitution independent of the field route shortfall?
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH-UNRESOLVED.decision_impact: Determines whether vendor AMI export health is a separate contributing cause requiring its own remediation path.
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH-UNRESOLVED.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned mdms-export access and compare AMI read events against disputed bills.
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH-UNRESOLVED.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db and route-log analysis without AMI read event data; mdms-export access remains ACCESS_PENDING/non-transient (recovery_decision seq 94).
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH-UNRESOLVED.resolution: E-11 shows AMI export itself functioned (1,184 of 1,240 reads were received before cutoff and exported successfully); estimate substitution is instead caused by billing import rejecting those exported reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, so AMI export degradation is not the independent contributor, though the import-rejection issue remains unresolved.

U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI.question: Does dispute ticket volume alone validly measure success, or could it be reduced by faster/auto responses without fixing the underlying billing defect?
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI.decision_impact: If volume alone is used as the success signal, a response-speed fix (not a billing-defect fix) could falsely appear to resolve the problem.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI.resolution_path: Cross-check dispute volume trend against root-cause tagging of resolved tickets in crm-tickets and billing-db to confirm volume reduction tracks actual defect correction.
U-DISPUTE-VOLUME-METRIC-VALIDI.safe_placeholder: Treat dispute-volume reduction (SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE) as a secondary TARGET; require the billing-defect-identified MUST criterion as the primary evidence of a real fix.

A-DEFECT-ONSET-AUGUST.statement: The billing defect's onset coincides with the August timing of the ticket surge rather than being a long-standing, slowly-surfacing issue.

A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-MINORITY-CAU.statement: The field route completion shortfall (E-05) is a genuine contributing cause limited to the minority of disputes tied to ESTIMATED reads, not the majority driver.
